summary_en: This Phase 2 study compares GLIADEL wafers placed at the surgical site with stereotactic radiosurgery in people with metastatic brain tumors that are removed surgically. After the tumor is removed, GLIADEL wafers are placed to cover the tumor bed, with the number based on cavity size, while the comparison group receives stereotactic radiosurgery within six weeks after surgery; the total length of treatment is not stated. The study aims to see whether adding GLIADEL works as well as surgery with radiosurgery in keeping the cancer from coming back, and a formal primary outcome measure is not stated.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 compara las obleas GLIADEL colocadas en el sitio de la cirugía con la radiocirugía estereotáctica en personas con tumores cerebrales metastásicos que se extirpan quirúrgicamente. Después de extirpar el tumor, se colocan obleas GLIADEL para cubrir el lecho tumoral, y la cantidad depende del tamaño de la cavidad; el grupo de comparación recibe radiocirugía estereotáctica dentro de las seis semanas posteriores a la cirugía, y la duración total del tratamiento no se indica. El estudio busca saber si agregar GLIADEL funciona igual que la cirugía con radiocirugía para evitar que el cáncer regrese, y no se indica una medida principal formal de resultado.
who_for: Age 18 or older (19 or older in Nebraska).
Metastatic brain tumor, up to four tumors, each up to 4 cm, with surgery planned at one site.
Karnofsky Performance Status of 60 or higher and RPA class I, II or III.
Estimated survival of at least 3 months, per the primary oncologist.
Labs adequate for surgery, INR 1.3 or lower, and able to consent and follow the protocol.
not_for: Prior treatment to the planned resection area, or prior whole brain radiation.
Lymphoma, germ cell cancer, small cell lung cancer, or anaplastic thyroid cancer.
Leptomeningeal disease or a neurodegenerative disorder such as dementia.
Tumor larger than 4 cm, or Karnofsky Performance Status below 60.
Bleeding disorder, or anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents that cannot be stopped for surgery.
